gap: No result ChatGPT got says how much energy these AC power banks actually deliver. PCWorld measured 78.78% of rated capacity from the Goal Zero Sherpa 100AC, about 74.6 Wh of its 94.7 Wh. It measured 56.6 Wh of 72 Wh from the Omnicharge Omni 20+. Techtest.org got only 48 to 60.5 Wh out of the Omni 20+ AC outlet.
standout_why: I opened four rival pages. Engadget (cited) has only Sherpa 100AC charge times for a MacBook Pro, iPhone and iPad, and no delivered-energy figure. It lists the mophie Powerstation Pro AC as tested but gives no numbers. Macworld (cited) gives rated capacity, recharge times and noise but no measured usable Wh. GeekChamp (cited) says it has no measured figures and uses a planning estimate of Wh × 0.80. ThunderboltLaptop says 'We did not test any of these banks' and repeats Amazon listing claims. None of them puts named-lab delivered Wh or AC-side efficiency side by side for the candidates.
decides: This backs the Sherpa 100AC as the flight-legal pick over the Omni 20+. Both have 100 W AC outlets, but the Sherpa delivered about 74.6 Wh in PCWorld's test and the Omni 20+ delivered 56.6 Wh. Through its AC outlet the Omni gave only 48 to 60.5 Wh in techtest.org's test, so the Omni carries roughly a quarter less usable energy. For the station tier, measured AC output was about 210 Wh for the EcoFlow RIVER 3 (StorageReview) and 231 Wh for the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 (The Technology Man). The page can use these numbers for real laptop-charge counts instead of rated Wh. One caveat: the PCWorld tests are from 2018 and 2019 and may not match the current hardware revisions.

findings.label: Share of rated capacity delivered (PCWorld efficiency test)
findings.source_title: Goal Zero Sherpa 100AC battery pack review (PCWorld, Jason Cipriani, 2018-12-20)
findings.note: Measured by Jason Cipriani in PCWorld's standard battery efficiency test. The procedure is not described on the page; it points to a separate roundup. I calculated 94.7 × 0.7878 = 74.6 Wh. The test covers the 2018 model, and the article doesn't say which hardware revision it was.

findings.label: Recharge time (PCWorld)
findings.value: 2 h 15 min with a 65 W USB-C adapter
findings.source_title: Goal Zero Sherpa 100AC battery pack review (PCWorld, Jason Cipriani, 2018-12-20)
findings.note: The same review says it took over 12 hours with a Samsung adapter.

findings.label: MacBook Pro charge (Engadget)
findings.source_title: The best laptop power banks for 2026 (Engadget, Amy Skorheim, updated 2026-01-12)
findings.note: Engadget is already cited in the chats, so this isn't new. The same tests took an iPhone 15 from 0 to 100% in 1 h 49 min with 83% left in the bank, and an iPad Air from 4 to 100% in 2 h 11 min with 62% left. No delivered Wh is given.

findings.label: Energy delivered (PCWorld efficiency test)
findings.source_title: OmniCharge Omni 20+ power bank review (PCWorld, Jason Cipriani, 2019-07-01)
findings.note: PCWorld says this is below the 82.28% average of the packs it has tested. The output port used isn't stated. Recharge measured at 1 h 40 min from empty with a USB-C wall charger.

findings.label: Energy delivered through the AC outlet (techtest.org)
findings.value: 48 to 60.5 Wh of 71 Wh rated (about 68 to 85%)
findings.source_title: Die Omnicharge Omni 20+ im Test, Power Delivery + Steckdose = Erfolg? (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2020-08-27)
findings.note: Michael Barton tested the EU 230 V unit and gives the result as a range; the load isn't stated. I calculated 48/71 = 67.6% and 60.5/71 = 85.2%. He confirms the outlet puts out a modified sine wave. At an 85 W load the unit shut down from heat with about 40% charge left. Recharge from 0 to 100% took about 2 h.

findings.label: Phone charge delivered (Cult of Mac)
findings.value: +342% total battery on an iPhone 14 Plus over several runs
findings.source_title: mophie powerstation pro AC review (Cult of Mac, Ed Hardy, 2023-03-30)
findings.note: No measured Wh. After an hour of charging at 41 W, two of the four LEDs were lit, and a full recharge took 'several hours'.

findings.label: AC runtime and recharge (The Gadgeteer)
findings.value: About 1 h running a 43-inch Toshiba 4K TV on AC; a little over 3 h to recharge via 60 W USB-C
findings.source_title: mophie powerstation pro AC portable power bank review (The Gadgeteer, Steve Holt, 2023-05-23)
findings.note: Steve Holt says the TV 'requires 100W', but he didn't measure what it actually drew, so the runtime can't be converted to Wh.

findings.label: Energy delivered before shutdown (StorageReview)
findings.note: Corinne O'Brien ran it with a 300 W fan as the load; the page doesn't say whether it was on the AC or DC output. I calculated 210/245 = 85.7%. Refilling to 100% took 270 Wh from the wall, peaking at 322 W in fast-charge mode.

findings.label: Usable energy on AC and DC (The Technology Man)
findings.value: 231 Wh on AC (about 80%) and 244 Wh on DC (about 85%), of 288 Wh rated
findings.source_title: This £189 Bluetti Elite 30 V2 Power Station Is Better Than I Expected (The Technology Man, Gidon, 2025-12-23)
findings.note: Gidon tested a UK unit with a constant AC load of unstated wattage and calls 80% 'a little below average'. With Eco mode off, the AC output drained the battery from 100% to 19% in 12 h, roughly 19 W of idle draw. In Turbo mode it recharged to 80% in about 40 min and to full in 51 min.
